Previously owned by Nordic Capital funds, it listed on Nasdaq Stockholm in 2024 (ticker NOBA). Customers are mainstream consumers rather than businesses. South Korean financial holding company formed in 2019 that owns Woori Bank, Woori Card, Woori Financial Capital, Woori Investment Bank and Woori Asset Management, and added life insurance units in 2024. Woori Bank traces its origins to 1899 and serves retail customers, small businesses and large corporates in Korea, with overseas branches in Asia, the US and Europe. Revenue is mainly net interest and fee income. Listed in Seoul and as an ADR in New York. Well known domestic consumer brand and already active in sports sponsorship.

US bank holding company behind First Business Bank, a commercial bank serving privately held small and mid-sized businesses, owners and executives with loans, deposits, treasury management and equipment finance. Operates in Wisconsin (Madison, Milwaukee), Kansas City and Phoenix, and added Alabama through Alterra Bank. Holding company First Business Financial Services trades on Nasdaq as FBIZ and manages roughly 3.5 billion dollars of assets. Regional B2B-focused bank with modest consumer visibility outside its local markets.

Mexican financial group owning Banco Invex, a brokerage, asset manager and trust business, which also issues co-branded credit cards, notably the Volaris airline card. It serves corporate, wealth and retail clients, and runs one of Mexico's larger trust (fiduciary) operations. The group is privately controlled through its holding company Invex Controladora and its shares are listed in Mexico. Mid-sized financial brand with modest consumer recognition through its co-branded cards.

Bank holding company for Royal Business Bank, a Los Angeles community bank that focuses on Chinese-American and Asian-American households, entrepreneurs and small businesses. It offers commercial real estate, business and residential mortgage loans, deposits and trade services through branches in California, Nevada, New York, New Jersey, Illinois, and Hawaii, with roughly 4 billion dollars of assets. Listed on Nasdaq (RBB). Strong niche community recognition, little general consumer profile.

Danish regional bank in Aalborg offering retail, business and wealth banking through about 50 branches, with a strong position in North Jutland and Danish retail customers, and a large mortgage and leasing activity through partners. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (SPNO) and among Denmark's larger listed banks. It agreed in 2024 to be acquired by Nykredit, with the deal closing in 2025. Well-known Danish consumer bank brand, historically a sponsor of local sports and football.

Canadian analytics company based in London, Ontario, tagged under analytics, lending and property. Likely sells data or software to lenders and real estate users, but the input does not confirm products or customers. The record is flagged as listed; scale and ownership are not known. Low expected consumer visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Small US community bank holding company (Bancorp 34), operating Bank 34 with branches in Arizona and New Mexico and serving local households, small businesses and real estate borrowers with deposits, mortgages and commercial loans. It was formed from a savings bank conversion and trades on Nasdaq (BCTF). Under 1 billion dollars of assets. Local financial brand with low national visibility.

Indian private-sector bank headquartered in Mumbai (formerly Development Credit Bank), serving retail customers, small businesses and agricultural borrowers via over 400 branches in India, with products such as mortgages, gold loans, vehicle loans, and savings accounts. Revenue comes from lending spread and fees. Listed on NSE and BSE (DCBBANK), with a mid-sized balance sheet. Moderately known regional consumer bank brand.

BIDV (Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam) is one of Vietnam's largest state-controlled commercial banks, offering retail, corporate and investment banking, with a large branch network across the country, a presence in Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar and Russia, and a stake in BIDV Insurance and securities units. Founded in 1957, it is listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (BID), with the State Bank of Vietnam as majority owner and Korea's KEB Hana Bank a strategic shareholder. Large consumer-facing banking brand in Vietnam with sports and community sponsorship activity.

Security Bank is one of the Philippines' leading universal banks, offering consumer, corporate and treasury services, including savings and credit cards, loans, wealth management and a digital bank, with a branch network across the Philippines. Founded in 1951, it is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (SECB) and is majority owned by the Philippines' Sy-family and Securities Investment Corp. Consumer-facing banking brand with moderate recognition in the country, and local sponsorship in sports and events.

Fotolia was a stock photography marketplace, based in New York with roots in Paris, which sold royalty-free photos, illustrations and videos contributed by a global community of photographers, to designers, agencies and publishers. Founded in 2004, it was bought by Adobe in 2014 for about 800 million dollars and integrated into Adobe Stock, after which the Fotolia brand was retired. Once widely used by creative professionals, it no longer exists as a standalone company.

Commercial bank headquartered in Blantyre, one of the two or three largest banks in Malawi, offering retail and corporate banking, savings and current accounts, loans, trade finance, cards and mobile banking through a national branch network. Customers are individuals, small businesses, corporates and government bodies, paid through interest margins and fees. Founded in 1971, listed on the Malawi Stock Exchange, with Press Corporation as the controlling shareholder. Well-known domestic brand with strong local awareness, but its reach is limited to Malawi and a small economy.

Vietnamese joint-stock commercial bank, branded LPBank since 2024 and formerly LienVietPostBank, with its network built on the Vietnam Post offices and listed on Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (LPB). It offers retail and SME banking, deposits, loans, cards, digital banking and remittances through hundreds of branches and post-office counters, with total assets above VND 400 trillion. Customers are individuals and small firms across Vietnam. Recognisable domestic retail bank brand, with moderate to high national awareness.

Chinese consumer finance technology company based in Shanghai that uses data analytics to match borrowers with lending partners. Its Vcredit app offers small cash loans and instalment credit to individuals, and it also provides credit risk services to banks and microlenders. Revenue comes from loan facilitation and technology service fees. It operates mainly in China, where tighter regulation of online lending has constrained the business. Recognised in Chinese consumer credit but regulation limits consumer brand marketing, and it has no presence outside China.

Export Import Bank of Bangladesh, a commercial bank founded in 1999 and headquartered in Dhaka, operating on Islamic Shariah principles. It provides retail, SME and corporate banking, trade finance, remittance and agricultural financing through over 100 branches and ATMs, and it is listed on the Dhaka and Chittagong stock exchanges. Customers are Bangladeshi individuals and businesses, with income from profit-sharing margins and fees. Known as a mid-sized private commercial bank in Bangladesh, with moderate domestic brand awareness.

South Korean financial holding company, KB Financial Group, based in Seoul and listed on the NYSE and Korea Exchange, operating KB Kookmin Bank (the largest retail bank in Korea), KB Securities, KB Insurance and KB Kookmin Card. Customers are retail and corporate clients, with assets above KRW 700 trillion. Founded 2008. Very strong domestic consumer brand and visible in sport sponsorship in Korea.

Turkish private bank headquartered in Istanbul, founded in 2012, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, payments, trade finance and private banking through a network of branches in Turkey's main cities. It has been owned by the Lebanese Bank Audi group, which has put it up for sale in recent years. Customers are Turkish individuals and companies. A mid-sized lender within the Turkish banking market, with moderate local brand awareness and no international retail presence.

China International Capital Corporation, Beijing-based investment bank founded in 1995 as a joint venture with Morgan Stanley and later owned by Central Huijin, Tencent and others. It provides investment banking, equities brokerage, asset management and wealth services, and ranks among China's leading IPO underwriters. Listed in Hong Kong (3908) and in mainland China. Brand known in finance circles rather than among the public.

Chinese merchant acquiring and payment services company based in Shanghai, a subsidiary of China UnionPay, the national bank-card network, providing point-of-sale terminals, merchant onboarding, payment processing and customer service for shops and businesses across China. Revenue comes from fees per transaction and equipment services. B2B payments brand, although the UnionPay logo itself is widely recognised among consumers in China and by Chinese travellers abroad.

B2B payments infrastructure, with little consumer awareness, although it sits within the Visa group.

UK specialist lender based near Manchester, Together Financial Services, offering secured loans, bridging finance, buy-to-let mortgages and development finance to individuals and property investors, including borrowers who find it hard to get a bank loan. Chinese online lending marketplace, Rong360, based in Beijing, that let consumers and small businesses compare loans and credit cards from banks and lenders, earning commissions from financial partners. Customers are small and mid-sized businesses paying rent, suppliers, tuition and taxes. Founded in 2009 by Eliot Buchanan, it later went through financial restructuring. B2B payments brand with moderate awareness among small business owners.

Brazilian bank, Banco PAN, based in Sao Paulo and listed on the B3 (BPAN4), owned jointly by Banco BTG Pactual and Caixa Economica Federal. It focuses on consumer credit, including payroll-deductible loans, vehicle finance and credit cards, and runs a digital banking app. Customers are mostly lower and middle income Brazilians. Moderately known consumer finance brand in Brazil, with limited advertising profile and a modest sponsorship history.

US bank holding company based in Englewood, Colorado, parent of InBank, which provides commercial and personal banking, mortgage and agricultural lending to customers in Colorado, New Mexico, Wyoming and Kansas. Shares are traded over the counter. Revenue comes from interest income and fees, and the bank has grown through acquisitions of small community banks. Regional bank brand with limited awareness beyond its markets.

Indian small finance bank, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, based in Bengaluru and listed on the NSE and BSE, offering microloans, savings accounts, deposits and housing and MSME loans, mainly to underbanked customers and small businesses in India. It grew out of the Ujjivan microfinance company and operates hundreds of branches in many states. Customers are low-income households and small traders. Recognised consumer finance brand in India, though regional and focused on rural and semi-urban markets.

Chilean bank, Banco Itau Chile, based in Las Condes, Santiago, formed when Itau Unibanco of Brazil took control of CorpBanca in 2016, offering retail, corporate, investment and wealth banking in Chile and Colombia. Listed in Santiago and on the NYSE. Customers are individuals, companies and institutions, with assets of tens of billions of dollars. A major mid-sized Chilean bank, well known domestically though with a lower profile than the market leaders.

Indian housing finance company, Can Fin Homes, based in Bengaluru and listed on the NSE and BSE, promoted by Canara Bank, which provides home loans and loans against property to salaried and self-employed households, mostly in south India. Founded in 1987. It operates through a network of branches and has a loan book of several hundred billion rupees. Strong regional brand in housing finance, advertising largely through banks and local media.

Louisiana bank holding company, Home Bancorp, based in Lafayette and listed on Nasdaq (HBCP), parent of Home Bank, which provides consumer and commercial banking, mortgages and wealth management through dozens of branches in Louisiana, Texas and Mississippi. Founded in 1908. Total assets are around USD 3.3 billion. Customers are individuals and local businesses. Regional bank brand with local community sponsorship, but small national profile.

Pennsylvania bank holding company, LINKBANCORP, based in Camp Hill and listed on Nasdaq (LNKB), parent of LINKBANK, which offers commercial and consumer banking, using a branch-light model, in central Pennsylvania, Philadelphia and nearby areas. It merged with Partners Bancorp in 2023, adding branches in Maryland and Delaware. Total assets are about USD 3 billion. Regional community bank with limited name recognition outside its markets.

New Jersey bank holding company, Northfield Bancorp, based in Woodbridge and listed on Nasdaq (NFBK), parent of Northfield Bank, which offers retail and commercial banking, multifamily and commercial real estate lending in New Jersey, Staten Island, Brooklyn and Pennsylvania through dozens of branches. Founded in 1887. Total assets are about USD 5.5 billion. Customers are local households and property investors. Regional bank with local awareness and community sponsorship.

Virginia bank holding company, Chain Bridge Bancorp, based in McLean and listed on the NYSE (CBNA) since a 2024 IPO, parent of Chain Bridge Bank, which provides banking, treasury and trust services to individuals, businesses and political campaigns and committees in the Washington DC area. Customers also include political organisations. Founded in 2006. Small, specialised bank with low public profile outside Washington.

Colorado-based wealth management and banking group, First Western Financial, listed on Nasdaq (MYFW), which provides integrated wealth planning, trust, investment and private banking services to high-net-worth individuals, families and businesses in Colorado, Arizona, Wyoming, Montana and California. Assets under management are about USD 7 billion. Founded in 2002. Boutique financial brand with a regional high-net-worth profile and few consumer sponsorship ties.

Indian software company, Newgen Software Technologies, based in New Delhi and listed on the NSE and BSE, selling low-code process automation, content management and customer communication platforms to banks, insurers, governments and healthcare organisations. Founded in 1992. Customers are enterprises in India, Asia, Africa, Europe and the US. B2B software brand with good recognition among bank technology buyers but none among consumers.
